Further studies using independent tissue cohorts, mechanistic gene perturbation, direct target-engagement assays, and in vivo validation are required.

articles.title: Metronidazole derivatives and phenolic compounds as potential adjuvants against bacterial resistance mediated by the MepA efflux pump in the Staphylococcus aureus K2068 strain.
articles.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus is a Gram-positive pathogen that possesses resistance factors responsible for the occurrence of several diseases, including those affecting the airways and gastrointestinal tract, causing osteomyelitis and systemic infections that increase mortality rates. Metronidazole is a drug with antiparasitic and antibacterial activity, and the phenolic compounds eugenol, dihydroeugenol, guaiacol, and phenol exhibit several therapeutic activities, one of which is antibacterial. Thus, eight compounds were synthesized by linking metronidazole with the aforementioned compounds, forming substances designated AD1-AD8. This study aimed to investigate the adjuvant potential of compounds AD1-AD8 in enhancing the action of ciprofloxacin and ethidium bromide against the S. aureus K2068 strain, considering the possible involvement of MepA efflux pump modulation, as well as to evaluate the direct antibacterial activity of these compounds. Broth microdilution assays and molecular docking studies were performed to assess antibacterial activity and inhibition of the MepA efflux pump. Compounds AD1-AD8 reduced the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of ciprofloxacin and ethidium bromide, with molecular docking results demonstrating a possible inhibition of the MepA efflux pump. Overall, substances AD1-AD8 were able to significantly potentiate the action of the antibiotic and ethidium bromide due to the probable blockade of the resistance mechanism. The obtained results indicate the potential of compounds AD1-AD8 as therapeutic adjuvants in combating efflux pump-mediated bacterial resistance.

articles.title: Associating p-phenylenediamine and p-toluenediamine with AML using a network toxicology-based approach.
articles.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a prevalent acute hematological malignancy among adults, notable for its unfavorable prognosis and relatively low survival rates. Evidence suggests prolonged exposure to substandard permanent hair dyes containing hazardous chemical agents may elevate cancer risk, including AML. However, the precise mechanisms underlying this carcinogenic association remain elusive. This research identified p-phenylenediamine (PPD) and p-toluenediamine (PTD), primary constituents of hair dyes, as highly carcinogenic substances potentially implicated as key drivers of AML linked to hair dye usage. Targets relevant to PPD and PTD were predicted using databases such as ChEMBL, SwissTargetPrediction, STITCH, and PharmMapper. Additionally, AML-related targets were retrieved from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and GeneCards databases. Core genes were isolated using weighted gene coexpression network analysis (WGCNA), least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), random forest (RF), and support vector machine (SVM) algorithms. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis confirmed the predictive accuracy of these critical targets. Immune cell infiltration analysis further elucidated potential associations between these targets and the AML immune microenvironment. To verify compound-target interactions and stability, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were conducted. Our computational predictions suggest that PPD/PTD may directly target PTPRC, suggesting a potential mechanism by which these compounds disrupt immune microenvironment homeostasis and could promote AML progression. These findings suggest that PPD/PTD exposure could promote AML progression, which warrants experimental validation.

articles.title: Real world evidence of second-generation antipsychotics for the management of behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This is the first systematic review synthesizing exclusively real-world evidence about the efficacy, acceptability, and tolerability of the most used Second-generation antipsychotics (SGAs) for the management of Behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSD). METHODS: Observational or quasi-experimental real-world studies were included involving participants with a mean age of > 50 years and an Alzheimer Disease, vascular dementia or mixed dementia diagnosis with BPSD. Interventions were SGAs. Suitable comparators were placebo, other SGAs or no-treatment. Studies with or without a control group were eligible. The primary outcomes were efficacy, acceptability and tolerability of SGAs for the management of BPSD. Certainty of the evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. PROSPERO (CRD420251143630). RESULTS: 17 studies were included, encompassing 7,748 participants. Of the evaluated SGAs, only risperidone (k = 5 studies, n = 1469) and quetiapine (k = 4 studies, n = 89) had sufficient real-world evidence for pre-post analyses. Two studies provided direct comparisons between risperidone and olanzapine. The pooled analysis showed no significant difference between risperidone and olanzapine on efficacy (SMD = - 0.19; 95% CI [ - 1.72, 1.34], I2 = 0%). BPSD appear to improve in pre-post studies with risperidone (SMD = - 1.36; 95% CI [ - 1.67, - 1.06], I2 = 82.1%), but not with quetiapine (MD: - 15.17; 95% CI [-32.18 to 1.84]; I2 = 89.7%). Quality of evidence was evaluated as very low on all outcomes. CONCLUSION: While evidence suggests that risperidone is associated with significant management of BPSD in routine clinical practice, quetiapine appears to show limited efficacy and lower acceptability; although apparent inefficacy may probably depend on small sample size. Despite lower discontinuation rates than those reported in clinical trials, the risks of EPS, falls, and mortality support the need for careful monitoring and individualized risk-benefit assessment. The very low quality of the evidence demands careful interpretation of findings.

articles.title: Response Heterogeneity to Gegen Qinlian Decoction in Ameliorating Insulin Sensitivity Is Associated With Osteopontin Expression.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to characterize heterogeneity in the anti-hyperglycaemic response to Gegen Qinlian decoction (GQD) in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) mice and identify response-associated candidate proteins. METHODS: T2DM mice were established by a high-fat diet and streptozotocin. Glycaemic control and response heterogeneity were assessed using blood glucose measurements. Serum insulin concentrations and pancreatic histomorphology were used as surrogate markers of pancreatic β-cell function (BCF). Insulin tolerance testing and an insulin-resistant HepG2 cell model were used to assess insulin sensitivity-related phenotypes. Candidate proteins were explored using liver transcriptomic analysis, network pharmacology and literature-informed candidate prioritization, followed by preliminary in vivo and in vitro validation. RESULTS: GQD produced heterogeneous anti-hyperglycaemic responses more closely associated with differences in insulin sensitivity-related measurements than with surrogate BCF indices assessed. Hepatic osteopontin (OPN) expression was elevated in T2DM mice and was selectively downregulated in the exploratory strong-responder subgroup. GQD treatment also reduced elevated OPN expression in insulin-resistant HepG2 cells. Serum OPN concentrations were positively correlated with blood glucose, indicating an association between higher OPN levels and poorer glycaemic outcomes. Wogonin and liquiritigenin were associated with OPN downregulation and increased glucose consumption, with PPARα representing a potential yet unconfirmed mechanistic link. CONCLUSION: OPN is associated with GQD treatment-response heterogeneity and may represent a candidate response-associated marker.

articles.title: Implementation of UGT1A1 genotype-guided dosing of irinotecan in Europe.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Uridine diphosphate glucuronosyltransferase 1A1 (UGT1A1) genotype-guided dosing of irinotecan presents an individualized dosing strategy that improves patient safety while maintaining therapeutic efficacy. Nonetheless, little is known about its implementation across Europe. This survey-based study provides an overview of UGT1A1 genotype-guided irinotecan dosing practices across Europe and characterizes how institutional, regulatory and practical barriers affect its broader adoption. METHODS: A 41-question survey assessing implementation, best practices and opinions related to UGT1A1 genotyping was distributed to healthcare professionals identified through professional societies and previous publications on pharmacogenetics or irinotecan, as well as through outreach to medical oncology departments and pharmacogenetic laboratories in Europe. The survey was open for participation for 10 weeks from January to March 2026. RESULTS: Of 345 healthcare professionals invited across 34 European countries, 119 (34%) from 107 centres in 27 countries participated. Respondents included clinicians (N = 40), laboratory experts (N = 34), pharmacologists (N = 33) and researchers (N = 12). Eighteen European countries reported varying extents of UGT1A1 genotyping for irinotecan treatment, with extensive pre-treatment implementation currently present in Italy and the Netherlands. Eight countries reported no testing. The most frequently cited drivers of implementation were the presence of clinical guidelines, reimbursement and test availability. UGT1A1 genotyping panels differed considerably across laboratories. CONCLUSIONS: While UGT1A1 genotype-guided dosing of irinotecan is increasingly being adopted in Europe, broad and uniform implementation is still limited and thus far unevenly distributed. Achieving European implementation of pre-treatment UGT1A1 genotyping for irinotecan will require the development and publication of clinical guidelines, test availability and coverage of genotyping costs.
authors: European Working Group for the Implementation of UGT1A1 Testing’

articles.title: Combined Methodological Approach to Examine Genotoxicity of Biocolourants Dermocybin and Dermorubin.
articles.abstract: Dermocybin and dermorubin are natural anthraquinone dyes which can be extracted from bloodred webcap (Cortinarius sanguineus) fungus. These biocolourants are suitable as textile dyes for several materials. The toxicity data related to these anthraquinones is limited which has hindered their wider use. Therefore, we studied their potential for genotoxicity using new approach methodologies (NAMs). Firstly, the flowcytometric micronucleus assay and the alkaline comet assay were performed from human hepatic HepG2 cells cultured in two-dimensional monolayer followed by the comet assay performed using NAM model three-dimensional spheroids from HepG2 cells. To study the genotoxicity in whole organisms and reveal possible sex dependent differences we used another NAM model: marine amphipods (Parhyale hawaiensis) and counted micronuclei from the extracted haemolymph. Both anthraquinones were non-genotoxic in human cells and aquatic organisms, which make them promising candidates for textile dyeing.

articles.title: Established replicative senescence alters cellular homeostasis and reduces susceptibility to uremic toxin-induced cytotoxicity in renal tubular epithelial cells.
articles.abstract: Population aging has become a major global health challenge, accompanied by a growing burden of age-related chronic diseases, including chronic kidney disease (CKD). Cellular senescence is a hallmark of renal aging and contributes to CKD progression. Although uremic toxins promote tubular injury and cellular senescence, how established senescent renal tubular epithelial cells respond to subsequent uremic stress remains unclear. Here, we established replicative senescence models in two normal renal tubular cell lines NRK-52E (rat) and HK-2 (human) and investigated their responses to the uremic toxins indoxyl sulfate (IS) and p-cresyl sulfate (PCS). Replicatively senescent cells exhibited increased senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity and p53/p21 expression, accompanied by disrupted autophagic homeostasis, enhanced NLRP3 inflammasome-associated inflammatory signaling, and altered expression of iron metabolism-related proteins. IS and PCS induced several of these molecular alterations in young cells, whereas their additional effects were limited in senescent cells. Notably, concentration-response analyses revealed significantly higher IC50 values in senescent cells following IS or PCS exposure, indicating reduced susceptibility to uremic toxin-induced cytotoxicity. Thus, established replicative senescence is associated with substantial basal molecular dysfunction but reduced susceptibility to subsequent uremic toxin-induced cytotoxicity. These findings reveal a dissociation between cellular dysfunction and cytotoxic susceptibility and suggest that this altered stress-response phenotype may favor the persistence of dysfunctional senescent tubular cells under chronic uremic conditions.

articles.title: The effects of permeation enhancers on drug permeability and ocular absorption into the rabbit eye with focus on posterior segment delivery via non-corneal route.
articles.abstract: Current treatments for retinal diseases rely heavily on intravitreal injections, highlighting the need for less invasive delivery approaches. Topical drug delivery via the conjunctiva-sclera route has shown promise for retinal targeting, but its successful application requires a thorough understanding of the permeation barriers and strategies to overcome them. Permeation enhancers (PE) are successfully used to improve gastrointestinal drug absorption and have also shown potential in ocular research. The purpose of this study was systematically evaluate the permeability of 13 small molecular weight drugs and bevacizumab across rabbit conjunctiva, sclera and sclera-choroid-RPE (SCR), and to recognize the most suitable PEs for ocular use. The achieve this, PEs were screened using MDCK II-wt cells followed by ex vivo permeability experiments using Ussing diffusion chambers. The most promising PE was chosen for in vivo study, where beta blockers containing eye drops and AF647-labelled bevacizumab were topically administered to NZW rabbits. The PEs C10 and SNAC showed the most potential for topical drug delivery, increasing small molecule permeation across rabbit SCR over 600-fold. While topically administered 2 mM C10 did not have major effect on small molecule drug concentrations in rabbit tissues, bevacizumab was detected in the retina at 240 min. The results indicated that the RPE is the most restrictive membrane in conjunctiva-sclera delivery of topical drugs to the retina. PEs show some potential to overcome this barrier, but adequate in vivo enhancement is difficult to reach. The potential of topical bevacizumab together with PE should be further investigated.

articles.title: Electrospun core-sheath nanofibers for transdermal drug delivery with combined UV imaging analysis.
articles.abstract: Coaxial electrospinning has been applied as a promising technique for improving the performance of transdermal drug delivery systems by having structural control over drug release and permeation. This study investigates the fabrication and characterisation of PVA-PEO coaxial electrospun nanofibers, using nicotinamide as the model drug. The study investigated the effect of PEO molecular weight on fiber morphology, mechanical properties, surface characteristics, wettability, drug release, and skin permeation. PVA-nicotinamide was used as the core material, while PEO with molecular weights of 300, 600, and 900 kDa was used as the shell polymer. The core-sheath formulations produced continuous and cohesive fiber mats, with the mean fiber diameter increasing from 823 ± 118 nm for C1 (300 kDa) to 988 ± 108 nm for C2 (600 kDa) and 1268 ± 281 nm for C3 (900 kDa). DSC and XRD analyses showed an absence of distinct melting endotherm and diffraction peaks attributable to crystalline NIC under the experimental conditions. The core-sheath structure improved the mechanical strength of the nanofiber mats, with tensile strength increasing from 5.6 ± 1.1 MPa for the 300 kDa PEO shell to 12.3 ± 2.4 MPa for the 900 kDa shell. Surface roughness and contact angle measurements showed that increasing shell molecular weight produced rougher surfaces with higher static contact angles. In vitro release studies showed that core-sheath fibers reduced the initial burst release and prolonged nicotinamide delivery compared with the monoaxial control. The 900 kDa PEO shell (C3) demonstrated the most sustained release, with 39.3 ± 7.3% of nicotinamide released after 2 h and 58.5 ± 14.6% after 8 h, compared with 96.1 ± 16.9% for C1 (300 kDa) after 8 h. Franz diffusion cell studies showed that NIC permeation decreased from 276.2 ± 59.1 µg/cm2 for the monoaxial control (C0) to approximately 95 µg/cm2 for C3 after 8 h. UV imaging showed a similar trend, with NIC permeation at 180 min decreasing from 81.1 ± 7.8 µg/cm2 (C1) to 71.9 ± 15.5 µg/cm2 (C2) and 60.7 ± 14.9 µg/cm2 (C3). Overall, these findings demonstrate the potential of varying PEO shell molecular weight to modulate drug release and permeation. The study also shows the integration of UV imaging as a novel technique to further provide valuable insight into drug transport across transdermal systems.

articles.title: Engineering directly compressible powders from polyphenol-rich aqueous extracts through pre-lyophilization co-processing with microcrystalline cellulose.
articles.abstract: The conversion of carbohydrate-rich botanical aqueous extracts into solid dosage forms remains a major formulation challenge because freeze-drying often produces sticky, cohesive, and poorly processable amorphous materials. This limitation is particularly relevant for polyphenol-rich extracts recovered from agro-industrial by-products, whose pharmaceutical valorization requires not only bioactive recovery but also the development of processable solid intermediates. Here, a pre-lyophilization co-processing strategy was developed to engineer directly compressible powders from a polyphenol-rich Olea europaea L. (OE) aqueous extract recovered from olive mill wastewater. The extract contained 17.43 g/100 g total polyphenols, mainly secoiridoid, verbascoside, and hydroxytyrosol derivatives ideally responsible for poor drying performance. Maltodextrin, maize starch, and microcrystalline cellulose (MCC) were investigated as formulation carriers. Unlike maltodextrin and starch, MCC produced dry, non-tacky powders with recovery yields up to 99.9% and enabled direct compression into tablets. DSC and XRPD provided descriptive solid-state characterization, with XRPD showing retained cellulose-associated diffraction signals together with diffuse scattering consistent with disordered constituents. . Among the investigated formulations, tablet T2 (OE:MCC ratio 3.3:1) provided the best compromise between extract loading, excipient burden, powder recovery, tabletability, and immediate polyphenol release, achieving complete dissolution within 30 min under simulated gastric conditions. Overall, this work demonstrates that pre-lyophilization co-processing with MCC represents an effective pharmaceutical engineering strategy to convert poorly processable polyphenol-rich aqueous extracts into directly compressible intermediates while supporting the valorization of olive mill wastewater through a processable solid dosage-form platform.

articles.title: Dose-adjustable amlodipine tablets engineered by semi-solid extrusion 3D printing at room temperature for point-of-care applications.
articles.abstract: Conventional technologies make it difficult to manufacture personalised oral dosage forms for thermosensitive active pharmaceutical ingredients. In addition, there are several drawbacks to the one-size-fits-all approach for hypertension management. For instance, commercial amlodipine products are available as amlodipine salts in limited fixed-dose strengths, which do not accommodate personalised dosing. This proof-of-concept study investigates the feasibility of using semi-solid extrusion (SSE) 3D printing at room temperature to fabricate dose-adjustable, antihypertensive drug susceptible to thermal degradation as oral solid dosage forms, with amlodipine free base as a model drug for point-of-care applications. A single amlodipine-loaded pharma-ink (2.5%w/w) was used to manufacture 3D printed tablets (printlets) containing 5, 7.5 and 15 mg of amlodipine free base by varying printlet dimensions. The printlets were characterised for physical properties, drug content, dissolution, solid-state properties and morphology using HPLC, SEM-EDX, DSC, PXRD, FTIR, Raman spectroscopy and solid-state NMR. Dose-adjustable printlets were successfully 3D printed at room temperature with acceptable drug content (96.8-104.9%), rapid disintegration (<5 min) and immediate drug release (t80% 9-22 min). Solid-state characterisation supports the physicochemical integrity of amlodipine following printing and drying, while HPLC showed no evidence of degradation products. The same pharma-ink enabled accurate fabrication of multiple dose strengths without reformulation. SSE 3D printing provides a simple approach for compounding personalised, dose-adjustable amlodipine free base tablets under mild processing conditions, avoiding its degradation. In addition, this approach could address the conventional manufacturing challenges associated with poor flowability of amlodipine base. The technology offers considerable potential for decentralised point-of-care manufacture of thermosensitive medicines and supports future implementation of personalised cardiovascular therapies.

articles.title: Systematic excipient selection as a tool to optimize solid state properties and aerosol performance of spray dried RNA loaded lipid nanoparticles.
articles.abstract: The advancement of RNA therapeutics, particularly small interfering RNA (siRNA), offers promising new approaches for the treatment of pulmonary diseases driven by aberrant gene expression and chronic inflammation like asthma and COPD. In this study, we systematically engineered dry powder inhaler (DPI) formulations containing low (0.8%) and high (2%) siRNA-loaded lipid nanoparticle (LNP) concentrations using spray drying. The matrix-forming excipients, lactose, mannitol and trehalose were combined with varying concentrations of L-leucine (3% to 30% relative to the sugar or sugar alcohol) and trileucine (3%) as dispersion enhancers. The goal was to address key formulation hurdles: maintaining siRNA gene-silencing efficiency, optimizing solid-state properties, and achieving efficient aerosolization for pulmonary delivery. Lactose and trehalose-based spray-dried powders exhibited yields over 70% and preserved siRNA bioactivity, with gene silencing efficiencies exceeding 95% in vitro. Physicochemical characterization revealed that these formulations containing low to moderate leucine or trileucine content solidified in the glassy state, displaying glass transition temperatures over 76 °C and residual moisture levels below 7%, favorable for long-term stability and pulmonary delivery. In contrast, mannitol-based formulations were highly crystalline and less compatible with LNPs, resulting in low yields, larger, irregular shaped particles and poor aerosolization efficiency. In vitro aerosol performance was assessed using two breath-actuated DPIs in a laser diffraction inhalation setup. Our findings highlight that successful pulmonary delivery of siRNA-LNP powders not only depend on powder attributes but also on the interplay between formulation and DPI device. Optimizing excipient selection with regard to a device's powder dispersion principle is essential to achieve robust aerosol performance, efficient lung deposition, and preservation of therapeutic activity in solid-state siRNA-LNP dry powder formulations.

articles.title: Shaoyao Gancao Decoction alleviates renal fibrosis by disrupting the NETs-EMT positive feedback loop through glycyrrhizic acid and paeoniflorin.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Shaoyao Gancao decoction (SGD), a time-honored classic formula, possesses antioxidant and antifibrotic properties, but the mechanism underlying its antirenal fibrotic effect remains unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to evaluate the antirenal fibrotic effect of SGD on unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO) mice and to elucidate the underlying mechanisms involved. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The chemical constituents of SGD were characterized by UPLC-ESI-Q-TOF-MS, and the main blood-absorbed components were quantified using UPLC-TQ-MS. Antirenal fibrotic activity was assessed in mice with unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO), and key biological processes were identified by proteomics and verified by western blot analysis and immunofluorescence staining. Network pharmacology and cellular thermal shift assays (CETSAs) were used to predict and validate potential targets of the absorbed components. Four in vitro models, including TGF-β1-stimulated HK-2 cells, PMA-induced neutrophils, and two coculture systems, were used to investigate the mechanism underlying the effects of bioactive components by detecting the activity of the NADPH oxidase 2 (NOX2)/reactive oxygen species (ROS)/neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) axis, TβR1 signaling and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) markers, all of which were further corroborated in vivo. RESULTS: Seventy-nine constituents were identified in SGD, with GA and PA, the official quality markers specified in the Chinese Pharmacopoeia, as the predominant blood-absorbed and renal distributed components. The administration of SGD at 4.2 g/kg, 8.4 g/kg, and 16.8 g/kg mitigated renal injury and collagen deposition, with the efficacy of the high dose comparable to that of pirfenidone. Proteomics and network pharmacology revealed that SGD regulated oxidative stress, NETs formation, and TGF-β signaling. Molecular docking and CETSA validated NOX2 and TβR1 as the potential targets of GA and PA. Using NETs scavengers and TβR1 inhibitors as controls in vitro, combined with in vivo validation, we confirmed that GA blocks the upstream NOX2/ROS/NETs axis, while PA suppresses downstream TβR1 to inhibit EMT-mediated NETs, collectively disrupting the NETs-EMT positive feedback loop to restrain EMT, reduce ECM accumulation, and delay the progression of renal fibrosis. CONCLUSIONS: This study is the first to demonstrate the therapeutic effect of SGD on renal fibrogenesis and clarify its key molecular mechanisms. The bioactive components GA and PA from SGD separately target the upstream and downstream parts of the NETs-EMT positive feedback loop to synergistically block the vicious pathological cycle of renal fibrosis, providing experimental support for novel clinical indications and the clinical translation of SGD.

articles.title: The anti-rheumatoid arthritis activity of the aqueous extract of leafy branches of Juniperus indica is related to its regulation of the intestinal microenvironment and inhibition of joint inflammation.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a common autoimmune disease characterized by inflammation and damage to the joints. Juniperus indica (JI), a commonly used traditional herb, is often employed for the treatment of arthritis and nephritis. Nevertheless, the efficacy of JI for RA and the underlying mechanism by which it works remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to explore the therapeutic effects of JI in a rat model of RA. It further sought to elucidate the underlying mechanisms, with a particular focus on the intestinal microenvironment and joint inflammation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: RA was induced in rats using type II collagen combined with incomplete Freund's adjuvant to establish the collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) model. Following 28 days of JI treatment, therapeutic efficacy was evaluated by assessing paw swelling, articular damage, immune organ indices, and inflammatory responses. Additionally, fecal levels of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) were quantified using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC). Furthermore, metagenomic sequencing, real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction, and Western blotting were performed to explore the mechanisms by which JI ameliorates RA. Ultra-performance liquid chromatography coupled with Q-Exactive Orbitrap mass spectrometry (UPLC-Q-Exactive Orbitrap MS) and molecular docking analysis were employed to identify the potential active components of JI responsible for ameliorating RA. RESULTS: JI treatment significantly alleviated RA symptoms, as evidenced by improvements in articular and pedal bone damage, paw swelling, paw thickness, paw volume, arthritis index, immune organ indices, and inflammatory responses. JI treatment was associated with changes in gut microbial diversity, composition, and transkingdom correlations. Furthermore, JI treatment increased the mRNA expression of ZO-1, occludin, and claudin-1. Moreover, JI treatment was associated with increased fecal concentrations of acetic acid, propionic acid, and butyric acid, together with reduced expression of HDAC1, HDAC2, and NF-κB p65 in synovial tissue. A total of 29 chemical constituents were identified in JI. Subsequent molecular docking analysis revealed that components such as cynaroside, eriodictyol-7-O-glucoside, and chlorogenic acid exhibited particularly strong binding affinities with the HDAC2 protein. CONCLUSIONS: JI exerted profound therapeutic effects on RA. JI treatment was associated with altered gut microbial diversity, composition, and transkingdom correlations, and with restoration of the intestinal barrier. Moreover, JI significantly mitigated joint inflammation, and this effect may be related to increased production of beneficial SCFAs and inhibition of the HDAC/NF-κB signaling pathway. Components such as cynaroside, eriodictyol-7-O-glucoside, and chlorogenic acid are candidate constituents that may contribute to the observed effects of JI.

articles.title: Antimalarial activity of Croton caudatus Geiseler leaf extract and its ability to reduce experimental cerebral malaria pathogenesis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Croton caudatus Geiseler is widely used in traditional medicine to treat various ailments, including malaria. However, scientific evidences supporting its antimalarial activity and the associated molecular mechanisms, and its potential to reduce severe malaria complications are lacking. AIM OF THE STUDY: The present study was aimed to evaluate the antimalarial activity of C. caudatus leaf extract and its fractions, and to investigate the underlying molecular mechanisms. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Methanolic leaf extract of C. caudatus (CcLE) was fractionated into water (CcWater), butanol (CcBut), chloroform (CcChl), and hexane (CcHex) fractions. In vitro antiplasmodial activity was assessed against two different strains of Plasmodium falciparum (Pf): Pf3D7 and PfCam3.IR539T, alongside cytotoxicity and hemolysis assays. Phytochemical profiling of the most active fraction was performed by chemical fingerprinting. Mechanistic studies included β-hematin polymerization inhibition, hemozoin quantification, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) measurement. Acute oral toxicity and in vivo antimalarial efficacy were carried out in Plasmodium berghei (Pb) ANKA-infected BALB/c mice. Experimental cerebral malaria (ECM) studies were performed in Pb ANKA-infected C57BL/6 mice through the assessment of blood-brain barrier integrity, inflammatory marker expression, and immune cell infiltration analyses. Examining the gametocyte numbers and ex vivo exflagellation assays were carried out with Pb ANKA-infected mouse blood to assess the gametocytocidal activity. RESULTS: CcHex exhibited the highest antiplasmodial activity against Pf 3D7 (IC50 = 6.84 ± 0.61 μg/mL) without detectable cytotoxic or hemolytic effects. Phytochemical analysis suggested the presence of bioactive metabolites associated with antimalarial activity. CcHex inhibited β-hematin formation in a cell-free assay and reduced hemozoin levels in Pf3D7 parasites, supporting its potential to interfere with parasite heme detoxification. It also increased intracellular ROS levels in the parasites, suggesting the disruption of heme detoxification. Further, CcHex treatment reduced gametocyte formation and impaired male gametocyte exflagellation, indicating gametocytocidal activity. Acute toxicity studies demonstrated a favourable safety profile. In Pb-infected Balb/c mice, CcHex treatment produced ∼62% parasite suppression at 1000 mg/kg/day. Importantly, CcHex treatment could protect against ECM by preserving blood-brain barrier integrity, and significantly reducing the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α and IFN-γ), chemokines (CXCL9, CXCL10, and CXCR3), the adhesion molecule ICAM-1, and CD8+ T-cell infiltration in the brain. CONCLUSIONS: The present study demonstrates that C. caudatus, a traditionally used medicinal plant, possesses significant antiplasmodial activity, exhibits protective effects against ECM, and impairs male gametocyte exflagellation. CcHex showed potent antimalarial efficacy through inhibition of parasite heme detoxification, induction of oxidative stress, and modulation of host inflammatory responses. These results support the ethnopharmacological use of C. caudatus and highlight its potential as a source of bioactive phytochemicals for the development of novel antimalarials and adjunctive therapies against severe malaria.

articles.title: Danggui Buxue Decoction is associated with reduced diabetic kidney injury and tubulointerstitial fibrosis alongside modulation of GSK--3β/CCND1 signaling.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Danggui Buxue Decoction (DBD) is a classical traditional Chinese medicine formula traditionally used to tonify Qi and nourish blood, and has shown therapeutic potential in diabetic kidney disease (DKD). However, its protective effects against tubulointerstitial fibrosis and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: To determine the effects of DBD on diabetic kidney injury and fibrosis and assess the potential involvement of glycogen synthase kinase-3β (GSK-3β)/cyclin D1 (CCND1) signaling. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Network pharmacology, molecular docking and HPLC-DAD fingerprinting were combined with a high-fat/high-sugar diet plus low-dose streptozotocin-induced DKD rat model and high-glucose-treated HK-2 cells. Renal function, tubular injury, oxidative stress, inflammation, fibrosis-associated markers, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-like changes, excessive extracellular matrix (ECM)-related markers, and GSK-3β/CCND1 signaling were evaluated by biochemical, histopathological, immunohistochemical, immunofluorescence, RT-qPCR and Western blot analyses. Additional HK-2 pharmacological comparisons included LiCl, flavopiridol, and combined LY294002/IGF-1 treatments. RESULTS: Network pharmacology identified 148 overlapping targets of DBD and DKD, with GSK-3β and CCND1 as core nodes; molecular docking predicted compound-target interactions. DBD-treated rats had lower blood glucose, HbA1c, serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen levels, together with lower injury-marker measurements and collagen deposition than model rats. In rat kidneys and HK-2 cells, treatment was accompanied by higher GSK-3β Ser9 phosphorylation and CCND1 expression and changes in epithelial, mesenchymal and matrix-associated markers. In additional HK-2 comparisons, LiCl and DBD showed similar directional changes in GSK-3β phosphorylation and marker expression, while flavopiridol and LY294002/IGF-1 co-treatment produced differing responses during DBD exposure. CONCLUSIONS: DBD attenuated DKD-associated renal injury and tubulointerstitial fibrosis, accompanied by modulation of GSK-3β/CCND1 signaling, changes in EMT-associated markers, and reduced extracellular matrix (ECM) accumulation. These findings suggest that modulation of GSK-3β/CCND1-related signaling may contribute to the renoprotective effects of DBD in DKD.

articles.title: Total flavonoids from Gleditsiae Spina Inhibit JAK2/STAT3-Mediated PD-L1 to Suppress Liver Cancer Immune Escape.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Gleditsiae Spina, the dried thorn of Gleditsia sinensis Lam. (Fabaceae), is commonly used in traditional Chinese medicine for surgical disorders. It is traditionally prescribed to reduce toxic swelling and promote pus discharge, particularly for sores and carbuncles at an early stage or when pus has formed but has not been discharged. Its traditional application to toxic swelling and inflammation-associated lesions provides an ethnopharmacological rationale for investigating its modern pharmacological effects on inflammatory responses and host defense. Total flavonoids from Gleditsiae Spina (TFGS) constitute a flavonoid-enriched bioactive fraction; however, their activity against hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and relationship with immune-checkpoint regulation remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to systematically evaluate the anti-HCC effects of TFGS and to investigate whether its effects on tumor-cell apoptosis, migration, invasion, and PD-L1 expression were associated with modulation of the JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathway. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Network pharmacology and molecular docking were used to identify candidate bioactive compounds, potential targets, and signaling pathways associated with the anti-HCC effects of TFGS. An H22 tumor-bearing mouse model and HepG2 cells treated with 20% TFGS-containing rat serum were used to evaluate the effects of TFGS on tumor growth, inflammatory factors, the proportion of CD8+ T cells, and cellular proliferation, apoptosis, migration, and invasion. Western blotting, immunohistochemistry, and quantitative reverse-transcription PCR (qRT-PCR) were performed to assess JAK2/STAT3 signaling and PD-L1-related molecular expression. An IL-6-induced JAK2/STAT3 pathway-activation assay was further conducted to evaluate the regulatory effects of TFGS on this pathway and PD-L1 expression. RESULTS: Network pharmacology identified six candidate flavonoids and 98 common targets. KEGG enrichment analysis indicated that these targets were predominantly associated with the JAK-STAT signaling pathway and the PD-L1/PD-1 immune-checkpoint pathway. Molecular docking showed that the binding energies of the tested ligand-target pairs were below -5.0 kcal/mol, suggesting favorable predicted binding affinities of the candidate compounds for core targets, including JAK2, STAT3, and PD-L1. In vivo, the medium- and high-dose TFGS groups achieved tumor inhibition rates of 27.89% (P < 0.05) and 53.74% (P < 0.01), respectively. TFGS also decreased serum TNF-α and IL-6 levels and increased the proportion of CD8+ T cells. In vitro, 20% TFGS-containing sera derived from the low-, medium-, and high-dose groups produced HepG2 cell-proliferation inhibition rates of 6.24%, 15.69%, and 22.64%, respectively, with statistically significant inhibition observed in the medium- and high-dose groups. High-dose TFGS-containing serum increased the total apoptotic rate from 9.79% in the control group to 21.23% (P < 0.01) and reduced the wound-closure rate from 62.59% to 27.72% (P < 0.01). The numbers of invading cells were reduced by 46.2% and 67.1% in the medium- and high-dose groups, respectively (P < 0.01). Mechanistically, TFGS reduced the phosphorylation levels of JAK2 and STAT3, increased the Bax/Bcl-2 ratio, and downregulated PD-L1, MMP-2, and MMP-9 expression. In addition, TFGS-containing serum attenuated IL-6-induced upregulation of PD-L1 and SOCS3. CONCLUSIONS: TFGS inhibited HCC progression, promoted tumor-cell apoptosis, suppressed migration and invasion, and downregulated PD-L1 expression. These effects were accompanied by reduced phosphorylation of JAK2 and STAT3, suggesting that the anti-HCC activity of TFGS may be partly related to JAK2/STAT3-associated regulation of PD-L1 expression. Interpretation is limited by the medicated-serum approach, the use of a single HCC cell line, and the lack of direct functional validation of PD-L1 regulation. This study provides new pharmacological evidence for the ethnopharmacological value of Gleditsiae Spina and supports further investigation of TFGS as a multi-target natural-product candidate for HCC intervention.

articles.title: Integrated Transcriptomics, Molecular Dynamics, and In Vivo Validation of Novel Sesquiterpene Lactones from Monosis parishii (Hook.f.) H.Rob. & Skvarla as COX-2 Inhibitors for Rheumatoid Arthritis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune disease characterized by synovial inflammation and pannus-driven joint destruction. Current NSAIDs and DMARDs therapies control symptoms but carry gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, and hepatic risks with long term use. Monosis parishii (Hook.f.) H.Rob. & Skvarla (syn. Vernonia parishii), traditionally used as a root decoction for rheumatism and bone pain in Yunnan, China, is a promising source of alternative anti-arthritic agents. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study investigates the phytochemical profile of M. parishii leaves and branches and evaluates their antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-arthritic potential. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A new sesquiterpene lactone, verparishinolide A (1), and eight known compounds (2-9) were isolated and structurally defined by ESI-MS, HRESIMS, 1D/2D NMR and single-crystal X-ray diffraction, which established the absolute configuration of compound 1. Anti-inflammatory, antioxidant and anti-arthritic potential were evaluated using in vitro LPS-stimulated assays, carrageenan and CFA-induced in vivo models, and an integrated transcriptomic/molecular docking approach to identify a druggable target. RESULTS: Compounds 1 and 2 inhibited LPS-induced nitric oxide production and proinflammatory cytokines (IC50 = 6.41 and 7.01 μM) and demonstrated significant in vitro antioxidant activity (DPPH 84.71%, 74.11%; NO 76.66%, 83.33%; Fe2+ chelation 81.82%, 72.72%; OH 81.42%, 80.01%), findings that were subsequently confirmed in vivo through restoration of endogenous antioxidant enzymes (catalase, superoxide dismutase, peroxidase, glutathione) under dexamethasone and saline-controlled conditions. To prioritize a druggable target, rheumatoid-arthritis synovial transcriptomics from three cohorts was integrated with compound-specific target prediction: among 11 proteins at this intersection, PTGS2 (COX-2) combined the highest prediction probability with a 3.37-fold, cross cohort-concordant increase in RA, and was advanced to 200-ns molecular dynamics, where compounds 1 and 2 docked with scores of -5.87 and -5.14 kcal mol-1, with native-pose recovery validated at 0.912 Å RMSD. In carrageenan-induced acute inflammation compound 1 (10 mg/kg) reduced paw swelling by 78.52 ± 2.89%, and compound 2 by 75.57 ± 1.92%. In CFA-induced chronic arthritis, Dexamethasone produced the strongest suppression of paw inflammation, followed by compounds 1 and 2, both of which restored endogenous antioxidant enzymes (catalase, superoxide dismutase, peroxidase, glutathione) and reduced inflammatory markers (nitric oxide, thiobarbiturates, IL-6, COX-2) in paw tissue. Histological and immunohistochemical analysis confirmed these effects, showing reduced inflammatory infiltration and IL-6 expression together with preservation of mature collagen and tissue architecture, approaching the effect of dexamethasone, with compound 1 consistently the more potent. CONCLUSIONS: These findings identify verparishinolide A as a structurally novel, mechanistically supported natural COX-2-directed anti-inflammatory lead from M. parishii.

articles.title: Preclinical study of butein in diabetic nephropathy and its impact on Nrf2/HO-1/GPX4 antioxidant defence and TGF-β/Smad2/3 signaling axis in kidneys.
articles.abstract: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a common microvascular complication associated with diabetes mellitus. Butein, a naturally occurring chalcone derivative, exhibits a spectrum of pharmacological activities. However, its precise role in DN remains unexplored. Our study employed a combined bioinformatics analysis with experimental validation in a rat model of high-fat diet (HFD)/streptozotocin (STZ)-induced DN, using biochemical, histological, and molecular analyses. Empagliflozin was used as the reference drug. In this investigation, administration of butein significantly reduced alterations in renal function, mitigated renal pathological damage, and inhibited the expression of extracellular matrix (ECM) components in rats. Diabetes-induced blood glucose and lipid profile parameters were significantly decreased in the butein treatment groups. Butein treatment considerably reduced oxidative stress and ferroptosis by upregulating the Nrf2/HO-1/GPX4 axis while concurrently downregulating acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4). Moreover, butein exerted antifibrogenic effects via the TGF-β1/Smad2/3 signaling and matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), thereby regulating the expression of ECM proteins. Additionally, treatment with butein markedly reduced the elevated levels of inflammatory factors, including TNF-α, IL-1β, COX2, and the pro-apoptotic factor caspase-3. Butein treatment markedly reduced the TUNEL-positive apoptotic cells in the kidneys. Further findings revealed that butein effectively reduced phosphorylation in the PI3K/AKT/GSK3β axis. Collectively, the findings suggest new potential targets for DN treatment, and the nephroprotective effect of butein is mediated by regulation of the PI3K/AKT/GSK3β, Nrf2/HO-1/GPX4, and TGF-β/Smad2/3 signaling axis.

articles.title: Glucocorticoid receptor drives the protective effects of contignasterol and contignasterines from Neopetrosia cf. rava.
articles.abstract: The glucocorticoid-like marine compounds contignasterol, contignasterine A, and contignasterine B, isolated from the marine sponge Neopetrosia cf. rava, have previously shown anti-inflammatory effects, although their mechanism of action remains unclear. This study aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying the protective activity of these compounds in inflammatory conditions. First, their effect on macrophage phenotype was evaluated in lipopolysaccharide-activated RAW 264.7 cells. Compounds modified macrophage polarization, as evidenced by the increase in intermediate-associated phenotype and the cytokines profile secretion. In the case of contignasterines A and B, this response was related to the induction of glucocorticoid receptor (GR) translocation to the nucleus. Contignasterol increased calcium entry in macrophages, suggesting the involvement of non-genomic pathways. Then, compounds were tested in an in vitro simulation of ischemia/reoxygenation injury in BV2 microglial cells. The metabolites preserved cell viability, reduced reactive oxygen species, and maintained mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm). Under these conditions, only contignasterine B increased GR nuclear levels, whereas contignasterol and contignasterine A showed no effects. Therefore, the involvement of mitochondrial GR signaling in the protective response of compounds was evaluated. Inhibition of mitochondrial GR with tubastatin A suppressed the effects of compounds in ΔΨm, which was confirmed by western blot of mitochondrial fraction. Interestingly, differences found in GR modulation could be related to compounds structure, and the presence of a 2-aminoimidazole moiety could be essential for nuclear GR translocation. These findings suggest different modulation of GR signaling by each marine-derived compound and highlight their potential as promising anti-inflammatory drugs.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetics, systemic toxicity, and acute behavioural effects of the phenethylamine derivative 25E-NBOH in rats.
articles.abstract: 25E-NBOH (N-(2'-hydroxybenzyl)-4-ethyl-2,5-dimethoxyphenethylamine) is a potent 5-HT2A receptor agonist of the N-benzylphenethylamine (NBOH) family that has recently emerged on the recreational drug market. Despite a documented case of severe human intoxication and the known lethality of closely related NBOMe analogues, an integrated preclinical profile of 25E-NBOH remains lacking. We therefore investigated its pharmacokinetics, systemic toxicity, neuronal cytotoxicity and behavioural effects in rats. In male Wistar rats, serum and brain levels of 25E-NBOH and phase-I metabolites were quantified by LC-MS/MS over 24 h (5 mg/kg, s.c.). Acute toxicity was assessed in females using OECD 423, and neuronal cytotoxicity in primary cortical cultures by MTS assay (0.01- 500 μM, 24 h). Behavioural effects were evaluated at 0.2, 1 and 5 mg/kg s.c. (15 and 60 min after administration), all of which exceed doses associated with recreational use. 25E-NBOH was rapidly absorbed (serum Cmax within 5 min), with peak brain levels at 1 h and a brain/serum AUC ratio of 8.5. The elimination half-life was 3.2 h. Two demethylated metabolites also crossed the blood-brain barrier (brain/serum AUC 6.8-8.4). Systemic toxicity corresponded to GHS Category 3 (LD50 ≈ 200 mg/kg). In vitro cytotoxicity was moderate (IC50 = 32.4 μM). All three doses produced dose-dependent suppression of locomotion, increased thigmotaxis, and disrupted PPI, persisting at the 60-min onset. At high doses, 25E-NBOH caused marked behavioural suppression and acute systemic toxicity, highlighting potential risks associated with overdose.

articles.title: ATDP33605, a selective NOP receptor agonist, reduces cocaine self-administration in rhesus monkeys.
articles.abstract: The selectivity and efficacy of a small-molecule NOP receptor agonist, 2,3-Dihydro-N-methyl-2-oxo-3-[1-[(1R)-1,2,3,4-tetrahydro-5-methyl-1-naphthalenyl]-4-piperidinyl]-1H-benzimidazole-1-acetamide (ATDP33605) were characterized in vitro. Next, its effects on operant behavior maintained by food pellets or self-administered cocaine were evaluated in a group of 4 male nonhuman primates. ATDP33605 showed high affinity for human NOP receptors expressed in HEK293 cells (Kᵢ = 0.59 nM) and exhibited approximately 240-fold selectivity for binding NOP over MOP receptors. ATDP33605 also stimulated [35S]GTPγS binding to human NOP receptors expressed in HEK293 cells in a concentration-dependent manner, with an EC50 of 2.39 nM and a Hill coefficient of 0.85. The efficacy of ATDP33605 was comparable to N/OFQ, indicating that it functions as a full agonist at NOP receptors. In behavioral studies, acute intramuscular treatment with ATDP33605 dose-dependently reduced the self-administration of a peak unit dose of cocaine, albeit with some variability among individual monkeys. Doses of ATDP33605 that significantly decreased cocaine-maintained behavior (0.32 or 0.56 mg/kg) had little or only transient effect on food-maintained behavior in individual monkeys. Subsequent studies revealed that the effects of ATDP33605 were apparent over a range of cocaine unit doses. These findings demonstrate that selective activation of NOP receptors effectively suppresses cocaine self-administration in primates, supporting a critical role of NOP signaling in cocaine-reinforced behavior. Variability among individual subjects highlights the need for studies with larger sample sizes and female subjects. Importantly, this study provides the first evidence that a selective NOP receptor agonist can reduce IV cocaine self-administration in nonhuman primates, suggesting its potential therapeutic value for cocaine use disorder.

articles.title: Nicotine increases dopamine signaling in the nucleus accumbens in male Wistar rats.
articles.abstract: Nicotine is the primary tobacco alkaloid that reinforces tobacco use. Increase in extracellular dopamine levels within the nucleus accumbens (NAc) is believed to mediate the reinforcing effects of nicotine. Historically, microdialysis and in vivo voltammetry have been commonly used to monitor nicotine-induced dopamine increase with different temporal resolution and dopamine specificity. Fiber photometry coupled with GPCR-based dopamine sensors recently emerged as a versatile tool for monitoring dopamine signaling linked to drug and drug-related behaviors at a subsecond time scale and with high dopamine specificity. Studies with this technique have begun to uncover rapid dopamine dynamics induced by nicotine aerosol exposure and subcutaneous injection. Intravenous self-administration (IVSA) remains a commonly used behavioral assay for assessing the reinforcing effects of nicotine. However, dopamine dynamics associated with nicotine IVSA remains to be determined. The current study investigated nicotine effects on rapid dopamine dynamics in the NAc following both passive and volitional IV nicotine administration and pharmacological regulation of these effects by nicotine-related compounds. Passive IV infusion of nicotine at 0.06 mg/kg significantly enhanced rapid dopamine signaling in the NAc and such effects were abolished by pretreatment with mecamylamine, varenicline, or bupropion. Volitional nicotine IVSA at 0.06 mg/kg/infusion also increased dopamine signaling in the NAc that was time-locked to active lever press and cue light presentation for nicotine infusion. These results suggest that increase in rapid dopamine signaling in the NAc may underlie the effects of nicotine and that inhibition of such effects may contribute to the pharmacological effects of nicotine-related compounds.

articles.title: Human disease-associated V94M mutation causes partial loss of function by impairing the plasma membrane trafficking of the TRPC5 channel.
articles.abstract: The human transient receptor potential channel canonical 5 (hTRPC5) is a second messenger-gated, Ca2+-permeable cation channel that is abundantly expressed in the brain. Owing to its X-chromosomal localization, TRPC5 variants bear the potential of causing channelopathies in hemizygous males. We identified a valine 94 to methionine (p.(Val94Met)) missense variant in two brothers with a neurodevelopmental disorder. To investigate if this variant affects the protein function, we inserted that variant into the cDNA of hTRPC5, and performed Ca2+ microfluorometry and electrophysiological analyses during channel activation via G-protein coupled receptors or by exposing cells to the direct activator englerin A. In both assays, we found a partial loss of function in hTRPC5(V94M) compared to wild-type hTRPC5. Since V94 is located within the second ankyrin-like repeat, a direct impact on the regulatory voltage sensor-like domain or the central pore domain seemed unlikely. We therefore analyzed whether the assembly of tetrameric channel complex or its integration into the plasma membrane are affected. Confocal microscopy demonstrated that hTRPC5(V94M) is strongly retained in endomembrane compartments with an impaired forward trafficking to the plasma membrane and sub-plasmalemmal punctae. Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) measurements revealed lower FRET efficiencies between hTRPC5(V94M) subunits as well as between hTRPC5(V94M) and wild-type hTRPC5 channel subunits, indicating that the assembly of hTRPC5(V94M) into homo- or heterotetrameric channel complexes may be impaired. Based on the functional analyses that demonstrate a partial loss-of-function of hTRPC5(V94M), these findings highlight p.(Val94Met) as a probable cause of the neurodevelopmental phenotype of the two affected brothers.

articles.title: Supplementation with hyodeoxycholic acid alleviated senescence and promoted nerve repair in aged rats post-peripheral nerve injury through upregulating E2F2.
articles.abstract: The recovery of peripheral nerve injury (PNI) is less desirable in the elderly and the aging of Schwann cells (SCs) hindered the repair process. Targeting SC senescence and restoring their reparative competence represents a pivotal therapeutic strategy for geriatric nerve repair. We proposed that the serum metabolomic changes in young rats post-PNI might provide some clues involving in nerve repair. We found that five bile acid (BA) species were significantly reduced in the aged rats post-PNI. Hyodeoxycholic acid (HDCA) alleviated the senescence of SCs dose-dependently among the five BA species. HDCA also restored the migratory capacity of the senescent SCs. Mechanistically, our results uncovered that overexpression of E2F2 alleviated the senescence and migratory inhibition of SCs induced by H2O2, while knockdown of E2F2 weakened the anti-aging and nerve repair of HDCA in vitro and in vivo. Our study suggests supplementation with HDCA could be a potential interventional strategy for nerve restoration after PNI in the elderly.

articles.title: Itaconate alleviates intestinal inflammation and epithelial barrier disruption in Crohn's disease through S100a8/PI3K/AKT signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Crohn's disease (CD) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease defined by a multifactorial pathogenesis, for which therapeutic options remain limited. Due to its potent anti-inflammatory effects, itaconate (ITA)-a tricarboxylic acid cycle-derived metabolite with immunomodulatory functions-has garnered considerable research interest. This study sought to clarify the mechanism of ITA in CD. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Initially, serum metabolomic profiling was conducted in 32 patients with active CD and 32 healthy volunteers. Subsequently, TNBS-induced colitis BALB/c mice underwent pharmacological intervention, and harvested colon tissues were further subjected to multifaceted analyses to evaluate the therapeutic effects. KEY FINDINGS: Initially, we observed significantly reduced serum levels of ITA in individuals diagnosed with CD relative to healthy controls. Furthermore, in a mouse model of colitis triggered by 2,4,6-trinitrobenzenesulfonic acid, intraperitoneal administration of ITA markedly attenuated disease severity. This intervention also suppressed the generation of inflammatory cytokines and preserved the integrity of the intestinal epithelial barrier. Multi-omics analysis revealed that the protective effect of ITA was related to the suppression of the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. Furthermore, we identified the pro-inflammatory protein S100a8 as a key downstream target regulated by ITA. Subsequent validation experiments showed that modulating S100a8 could mimic the therapeutic effects of ITA, confirming that ITA partially alleviates CD by regulating S100a8 to inhibit the PI3K/AKT pathway. SIGNIFICANCE: This research unveils a new mechanism of ITA in alleviating CD and highlights its potential as a medical treatment in the future.

articles.title: PLAUR-associated pro-apoptotic responses to inflammatory BV2-derived sEV-enriched preparations: Implications for traumatic brain injury.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) causes secondary neuronal loss, but the contribution of microglia-derived small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) remains unclear. We investigated whether sEV-enriched preparations from inflammatory microglial cells promote pro-apoptotic responses in cortical neuronal cultures and assessed the involvement of Plaur, which encodes the cell-surface urokinase-type plasminogen activator receptor (uPAR/CD87). MATERIALS AND METHODS: We used a controlled cortical impact mouse model, reanalyzed the cortical stab-wound single-cell RNA-sequencing dataset GSE226207, and characterized sEV-enriched preparations isolated from lipopolysaccharide-stimulated BV2 cells using nanoparticle tracking analysis, transmission electron microscopy, and western blotting. Cortical neuronal cultures were exposed to these preparations and evaluated by TUNEL staining, immunoblotting, bulk RNA sequencing, and siRNA-mediated Plaur knockdown. KEY FINDINGS: Controlled cortical impact was associated with neurological impairment, neuronal apoptosis, and microglial/macrophage activation. The public dataset showed injury-associated transcriptional changes and predicted altered microglia-neuron communication. In vitro, BV2-derived sEV-enriched preparations increased TUNEL positivity, increased Bax, caspase-3, and PARP levels, decreased Bcl-2 levels, and induced apoptosis-related transcriptional programs, including Plaur upregulation. Plaur knockdown attenuated these molecular changes. SIGNIFICANCE: These findings support PLAUR-associated signaling as a candidate mediator of pro-apoptotic responses induced by inflammatory BV2-derived sEV-enriched preparations in vitro. Further in vivo validation is required to establish a causal role for endogenous microglial sEVs after TBI.

articles.title: Arsenic trioxide inhibits high-grade human B-cell lymphoma cell lines by targeting zinc finger domain of BCL6 and triggering proteasomal degradation.
articles.abstract: The direct pharmacological inhibition of oncogenic transcription factors remains a formidable challenge in drug discovery. Here, we report that arsenic trioxide (ATO), a clinical agent used for acute promyelocytic leukemia, functions as a first-in-class degrader of the B-cell lymphoma 6 (BCL6) oncoprotein by targeting its C-terminal zinc finger (ZF) domain. In high-grade B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (B-NHL) models, ATO potently inhibited cell proliferation, induced G1-phase cell cycle arrest, and triggered apoptosis. Unbiased thermal proteome profiling and functional validation identified BCL6 as a primary cellular target. Direct engagement was confirmed by cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA, ΔTm = 6.58 °C) and mutagenesis studies, demonstrating that ATO binds specifically to the ZF domain, leading to ubiquitin-mediated proteasomal degradation of BCL6. This degradation relieved repression of key tumor suppressors, including p53 and p21, recapitulating the cell-cycle and apoptotic phenotypes. Significantly, ATO exhibited robust antitumor activity in BCL6-driven xenograft models, reducing tumor growth in a dose-dependent manner without observable systemic toxicity. Our work elucidates a novel mechanism of action for ATO, revealing the therapeutic potential of targeting transcription factor ZF domains and providing a compelling, potentially translatable strategy for repurposing ATO in B-NHL and potentially other BCL6-dependent malignancies.

articles.title: miR-339-3p alleviates sevoflurane-induced cognitive impairment in aged rats and exerts neuroprotective effects in SH-SY5Y cells via targeting GRIN1.
articles.abstract: Sevoflurane (Sev) exposure is a major risk factor for cognitive impairment in elderly patients, and miRNAs play a key regulatory role in its pathogenesis; however, the role and mechanism of miR-339-3p remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the role of miR-339-3p on Sev-induced cognitive impairment and its targeted regulatory relationship with GRIN1. We established a Sev-induced cognitive impairment model in aged rats and a neuronal injury model in SH-SY5Y cells, detected the expression of miR-339-3p and GRIN1, examined the role of miR-339-3p on neuronal damage through functional assays, and validated the targeting relationship between the two using dual-luciferase reporter assays and rescue experiments. Following Sev treatment, miR-339-3p was markedly downregulated while GRIN1 was upregulated. Overexpression of miR-339-3p improved cognitive function in rats and alleviated apoptosis, oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses in cells. In vitro assays confirmed that miR-339-3p directly targets the 3'UTR of GRIN1, and GRIN1 overexpression partially reversed its protective effects. These findings indicate that miR-339-3p alleviates Sev-induced cognitive impairment in aged rats, with in vitro mechanistic evidence supporting its action through direct targeting and downregulation of GRIN1, offering a potential molecular target that may inform future research on anesthesia-related cognitive decline, although its direct clinical applicability requires further validation.

articles.title: ConK-1, a cyclooctylamine analog of Conorphin-39, produced potent analgesic and antipruritic effects with attenuated side effects.
articles.abstract: Traditional μ-opioid receptor (MOR) agonists are mainstays in pain management, while their clinical application is hampered by severe side effects. The κ-opioid receptor (KOR) has emerged as an attractive therapeutic target due to its potent analgesia and reduced addiction risk. Conorphin-39 (Bz-Pro-D.Arg-D.Arg-Gln-Cha-c[Cys-Cys]-NH2) is a selective and potent KOR agonist derived from marine cone snail conotoxins. However, its pharmacological activities remain incompletely characterized. Herein, we systematically evaluated its analgesic effects in Complete Freund's adjuvant (CFA)-induced inflammatory pain model and antipruritic effects in compound 48/80-induced acute itch model, respectively. To improve the druggability of Conorphin-39, we designed and synthesized the analog ConK-1 (Bz-Pro-D.Arg-D.Arg-Gln-Cha-cyclooctylamine) by replacing the C-terminal cyclic cysteine motif with a hydrophobic cyclooctylamine moiety. In vitro calcium mobilization assays demonstrated that ConK-1 exhibited 3.9-fold higher KOR agonistic potency compared to Conorphin-39. In addition, ConK-1 showed reduced recruitment of β-arrestin2 under the test conditions. Subcutaneous administration of both Conorphin-39 and ConK-1 produced KOR-mediated analgesic and antipruritic effects in mice. ConK-1 showed comparable antinociceptive potency in male and female mice with CFA-induced inflammatory pain. Neither compound increased immobility time in the forced swimming and tail suspension tests at analgesically effective doses. Critically, subcutaneous ConK-1 did not elicit motor incoordination. Taken together, this study identifies a promising scaffold for developing analgesic drugs with reduced side effects.

articles.title: Evaluation of a long-term human hepatocyte culture maintained in PowerHEP maintenance medium for drug clearance prediction.
articles.abstract: Clearance is a key pharmacokinetic determinant in drug discovery, but low-turnover compounds remain difficult to assess because conventional hepatocyte systems rapidly lose metabolic activity. In this study, we evaluated a long-term primary human hepatocyte culture supported by a commercially available maintenance medium that maintains hepatocyte viability and metabolic competence for up to 4 weeks in simple 2D cultures. Across 4 PHH donors, hepatocytes formed confluent monolayers within 3 days and maintained stable ATP levels through day 28. Targeted proteomics demonstrated that the major drug-metabolizing enzymes and transporters remained largely stable between days 4, 11, and 25; generally within <2-fold change in abundance. Consistently, probe substrate assays showed that CYP1A2, CYP2C9, CYP2D6, CYP3A4, and UGT activities were mostly maintained from day 6 to day 28 within approximately 2-fold of day 6 baseline, although some enzyme- and donor-dependent variability was observed. In clearance studies, all tested compounds achieved at least 15% parent depletion. Clearance estimates were reproducible across incubation windows, with Pearson's r of 0.98. For compounds primarily metabolized by CYP3A4, CYP2D6, CYP1A2, CYP2C9, and UGT1A1, predicted intrinsic clearance values showed good agreement with observed in vivo values, typically within 3-fold. In contrast, a smaller subset of pathways, exemplified by UGT2B7 and OATP1B-mediated clearance, displayed approximately 10-fold discrepancies between in vitro and in vivo intrinsic clearance. These proof-of-concept findings demonstrated the potential of PowerHEP maintenance medium-based hepatocyte cultures to support long-term PHH culture and clearance assessment across selected metabolic pathways. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This study provides a proof-of-concept evaluation of a PowerHEP maintenance medium-supported long-term 2D primary human hepatocyte culture system for hepatic clearance IVIVE. The system maintained hepatocyte viability and metabolic competence and enabled clearance measurement for compounds over extended incubation periods. These findings support further evaluation of the platform across broader chemical space and additional hepatocyte donors.

articles.title: Nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT) inhibitors selectively induce cell death in human glioblastoma stem cells: Perspectives for preventing glioblastoma recurrence.
articles.abstract: UNLABELLED: Glioblastoma recurrence, largely driven by chemo- and radiotherapy-resistant glioma stem cells, remains a major clinical obstacle. Although nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase is key to cancer metabolism, past clinical trials with systemic inhibitors failed due to severe toxicity and limited efficacy against the bulk tumor mass. This study investigates whether nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase targeting can be repurposed, shifting the focus from reducing primary tumor size to selectively eliminating patient-derived glioblastoma stem cells to prevent relapses. METHODS: We assessed nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase expression and metabolic dependence in patient-derived glioblastoma stem cells, standard glioblastoma cell lines, and non-malignant human cells (astrocytes, endothelial cells, and differentiated neurons). Cytotoxicity, apoptosis, and therapeutic selectivity of small-molecule inhibitors were analyzed alongside enzyme-silencing experiments. RESULTS: Patient-derived glioblastoma stem cells showed high nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase levels together with negligible nicotinate phosphoribosyltransferase expression, making them strictly dependent on the salvage pathway. Synthetic nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase inhibitors induced apoptosis in glioblastoma stem cells at nanomolar or picomolar concentrations, whereas non-malignant neural and vascular cells tolerated doses up to the micromolar range. Standard glioblastoma cell lines were considerably less sensitive, failing to reflect stem cell responses. Finally, genetic silencing of nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase mimicked inhibitor-induced toxicity, confirming target-specific action. CONCLUSION: These results reveal a clear therapeutic window for nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase inhibitors. Instead of broad systemic use against primary tumors, these agents could serve as targeted post-operative tools to eradicate residual stem cells and reduce the risk of glioblastoma recurrence.

articles.title: Strategic substitutions of agmatine reduce tactile hypersensitivity in peripheral nerve injury.
articles.abstract: The decarboxylated form of L-arginine, agmatine, inhibits neuroplasticity through inhibition of the N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor. We have demonstrated that central or systemic agmatine administration inhibits neuropathic pain behaviors. However, the options for the pharmaceutical development of agmatine are limited. To capitalize on agmatine's therapeutic potential, we designed a series of agmatine analogs. Systemically administered strategically substituted agmatine 1-4 (SSA1-4), agmatine, and positive control ligands were evaluated for reversal of tactile hyperalgesia in nerve-injured mice and rats as well as preclinical models of motor function, cardiovascular performance, and abuse liability, and the effects of SSA1-4 were compared between GluN2B-knockdown and control mice. Finally, a pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) model was developed. Intravenous delivery of SSA1-4 reversed neuropathic pain behaviors in both the induction and maintenance phases of neuropathic pain. Similar to agmatine and ifenprodil, the effects of SSA1 and SSA2 required the presence of the GluN2B subunit-containing N-methyl-D-aspartate receptors in mice. At doses that elicit antihyperalgesia, SSA1-4 and agmatine lacked effects in preclinical models of motor dysfunction, cardiovascular function, and abuse liability. The PK/PD modeling revealed that each compound exhibited distinct PK/PD profiles, and each compound was best described by a 2-compartment model. Through strategic substitution of the agmatine molecule, we have developed and characterized a line of new chemical entities that present a pharmacological profile comparable to that of the parent compound agmatine, including a wide therapeutic window without side effects common to analgesic medications. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: The concomitant pain and opioid epidemics have led to a call for the development of safe and effective pain-relieving therapies. This study developed and characterized a line of new chemical entities, the strategically substituted agmatine compounds, and demonstrates their analgesic efficacy with limited side effects.

articles.title: Retraction Note: Multifaceted therapeutic approach via thiazolidinedione-infused magnolol in chitosan nanoparticles targeting hyperlipidemia and oxidative stress in gestational diabetes mellitus in experimental mice.
Retraction Note: Transcription factor decoy oligodeoxynucleotides to nuclear factor-κB inhibit reverse passive Arthus reaction in rat.
Development and qualification of recombinant Göttingen Minipig CYP3A22 and CYP3A29.
articles.abstract: In vitro drug metabolism assays are essential in early drug development to evaluate drug disposition. These assays often use hepatic subcellular fractions and recombinant enzymes originating from both human and nonclinical species. Within this domain, cytochrome P450 (CYP) 3A enzymes are considered key players for drug metabolism. Although recombinant CYP3A enzymes are available for several nonclinical species, isoform-specific enzymes from Göttingen Minipigs remain unavailable. Therefore, recombinant Göttingen Minipig CYP3A22 and CYP3A29 enzymes were developed in Escherichia coli. Their catalytic functionalities were examined using probe substrates (i.e., benzyl-oxy-methyl-resorufin and Luciferin-IPA), and clinically relevant human CYP3A4 substrates (i.e., midazolam and testosterone) along with known inhibitors (i.e., ketoconazole and troleandomycin). Gene sequence comparison to domestic pig revealed sequence variations for both r-CYP3A22 and r-CYP3A29. BOMR metabolism was detected in both constructs, but only r-CYP3A22 metabolized Luciferin-IPA. r-CYP3A22 exhibited a higher apparent affinity for midazolam, with a lower Km and comparable Vmax to r-CYP3A29, whereas r-CYP3A29 showed a greater maximal metabolic capacity toward testosterone, with a higher Vmax and similar Km as compared to r-CYP3A22. Ketoconazole exhibited potent reversible inhibitory effects on testosterone and midazolam metabolism in both enzymes. Troleandomycin strongly inhibited both constructs in a time-dependent manner; however, an IC50 shift was only measurable for r-CYP3A22. These results provide important insights into Göttingen Minipig CYP3A isoform-specific functionality which are relevant for species selection in future nonclinical studies.

articles.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing identifies stem-like subpopulations and their gene signature in lung adenocarcinoma progression.
articles.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) demonstrates significant intra-tumor heterogeneity (ITH), which plays a critical role in disease progression and complicates therapeutic interventions. In the present study, we employed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to analyze cellular populations derived from stage I and stage III LUAD tumors, alongside matched adjacent normal tissues, with the objective of delineating malignant cell states and identifying tumor-propagating subpopulations. Unsupervised clustering analysis identified eight principal cell lineages, with epithelial cells predominating within tumor samples. Notably, advanced-stage tumors demonstrated a shift toward an immunosuppressive microenvironment, characterized by elevated T cell exhaustion and an increased presence of pro-angiogenic macrophages. Further stratification of malignant cells revealed eleven distinct subclusters, with stage III tumors enriched for invasive and immunosuppressive phenotypes. Pseudotime trajectory analysis identified evolutionary transitions from alveolar-like states toward squamous and stress-responsive lineages. Employing CytoTRACE to evaluate stemness independently of predefined markers, we identified subpopulations of cancer stem cells (sub-CSCs) predominantly in stage III tumors. These sub-CSCs exhibited heightened transcriptional heterogeneity and a core gene signature associated with cytoskeletal motility, immune regulation, metabolic reprogramming, and protein homeostasis. A four-gene panel derived from this signature demonstrated robust prognostic significance in independent LUAD cohorts. Collectively, these findings enhance the current understanding of stemness-driven tumor progression in LUAD and suggest potential therapeutic targets to address tumor heterogeneity.

articles.title: Raddeanin A is associated with enhanced anti-tumor efficacy of doxorubicin in a murine breast cancer model by modulating MDR1 expression.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Doxorubicin (DOX) efficacy in breast cancer is limited by multidrug resistance (MDR) associated with P-gp/MDR1. Raddeanin A (RA) shows antitumor potential, but its role in modulating MDR is unexplored. PURPOSE: To evaluate whether RA may potentiate DOX anticancer effects and to examine potential mechanisms potentially involving MDR1-associated efflux. METHODS: Synergy was assessed in 4T1 cells (MTT, colony formation, apoptosis, ROS, Nrf2/HO-1). Molecular docking and flow cytometry evaluated RA-MDR1 interaction and DOX accumulation. In vivo efficacy and cardiotoxicity were examined in a 4T1 xenograft model. RESULTS: RA was associated with DOX sensitivity (reduced IC50), synergistically suppressed proliferation, increased ROS/apoptosis, and was associated with downregulation of Nrf2/HO-1 expression levels. Mechanistically, RA was associated with reduced MDR1 expression and increased intracellular DOX accumulation, consistent with the possibility that RA may be associated with altered drug retention potentially related to MDR1. In vivo, RA + DOX combination was associated with improved tumor inhibition without additional systemic or cardiotoxicity (normal body weight, cardiac histology, CK/CK-MB). This was associated with enhanced apoptosis and reduced MDR1 expression, along with findings consistent with reduced Nrf2/HO-1 expression levels in tumors. CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that RA may be associated with reduced MDR1 expression and increased intracellular DOX accumulation, increased apoptotic signaling, and downregulation of Nrf2/HO-1 expression levels, as suggested by correlative and pharmacological data. These observations are consistent with the possibility that RA may serve as a potential adjuvant to improve DOX efficacy in breast cancer, although further mechanistic studies are required to establish causality.

articles.title: Patterns of proton pump inhibitor prescription: a retrospective study from a tertiary hospital in Saudi Arabia.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are overprescribed extensively.
